rows.name: APT_DEPLOY_KEY
rows.who_sets: No file in the repository. The value comes from the GitHub secret settings.
rows.read_by: Jobs `verify-testing-order` and `publish-apt` (`.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml`), job `publish` (`.github/workflows/positron-dice-deb.yml`)
rows.values: Text of an SSH private key for the user `aptuser` on the APT server (the server that holds the Debian package channels).
rows.default: Unset: no default. `publish-deb.yml` declares the secret as required when another workflow calls it.
rows.effect: `publish-deb.yml` copies it to `APT_SSH_KEY` for the step that lists the `testing` channel. Both workflows pass it as `SSH_PRIVATE_KEY` to the shared workflow `publish-apt.yml`.
rows.notes: The shared workflow is `positron-ai/github-actions/.github/workflows/publish-apt.yml`. It is not in this repository. A channel is one package repository on the APT server, for example `unstable` or `testing`.

rows.name: APT_SSH_HOST
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/list-apt-channel-packages.sh`
rows.values: Host name of the APT server (the server that holds the Debian package channels). The workflow writes `apt.positron.internal`. The script uses the text unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: the script stops with the message `APT_SSH_HOST must name the apt server`. An empty value gives the same result.
rows.effect: It is the host part of the SSH target `<user>@<host>`. On that host the script runs `aptly repo show -with-packages <channel>` to list the packages of one channel.
rows.notes: The script also needs `APT_SSH_KEY` and `APT_SSH_USER`. `ssh` runs with `BatchMode=yes`, `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` and a connect timeout of 15 seconds.

rows.name: APT_SSH_KEY
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/list-apt-channel-packages.sh`
rows.values: Text of an SSH private key. The workflow copies it from the secret `APT_DEPLOY_KEY`.
rows.default: Unset: the script stops with the message `APT_SSH_KEY must hold the deploy key`. An empty value gives the same result.
rows.effect: The script writes the key to a temporary file. It gives that file to `ssh` with the option `-i` to log in to the APT server (the server that holds the Debian package channels).
rows.notes: The value is a secret. The temporary file has mode `600`. The script removes the file on exit. `ssh` uses only this key (`IdentitiesOnly=yes`). The script also needs `APT_SSH_HOST` and `APT_SSH_USER`.

rows.name: APT_SSH_USER
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/list-apt-channel-packages.sh`
rows.values: User name on the APT server (the server that holds the Debian package channels). The workflow writes `aptuser`. The script uses the text unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: the script stops with the message `APT_SSH_USER must name the apt server user`. An empty value gives the same result.
rows.effect: It is the user part of the SSH target `<user>@<host>`. The script logs in as this user to list the packages of one channel.
rows.notes: The script also needs `APT_SSH_KEY` and `APT_SSH_HOST`.

evidence.quote: : "${APT_SSH_USER:?APT_SSH_USER must name the apt server user}"

rows.name: BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/background-check.sh`
rows.values: Path of a directory. The script uses the text unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: the script uses `RUNNER_TEMP`. Without `RUNNER_TEMP` it uses `TMPDIR`. Without `TMPDIR` it uses `/tmp`. An empty value counts as unset.
rows.effect: It sets the root directory for the state of each background check (a slow check that the script runs in the background of a job). The state of one check is in `background-check-<NAME>`.
rows.notes: When `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is set, the script first appends `background-checks-<run id>-<attempt>-<job>` to the root. `bin/ci/README.md` asks matrix jobs with a shared temporary directory to set separate roots.

rows.name: BASE_REF
rows.read_by: Step `Generate unified benchmark report` of job `benchmark-report` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Branch name. The workflows write `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}`, the base branch of the pull request. The step uses the text unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: no default. The step sets the variable in its own `env` block on every run.
rows.effect: The step passes it to `bin/ci/generate_benchmark_report.sh` as the fourth argument, the reference branch. The script uses the branch to find the commit that the benchmark report compares with.
rows.notes: When the value equals `DEFAULT_BRANCH`, the step passes empty text for this argument and for `BASE_SHA`. The report then has no reference commit. The job runs only for `pull_request` events.

rows.name: BASE_SHA
rows.read_by: Step `Generate unified benchmark report` of job `benchmark-report` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Git commit id. The workflows write `${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}`, the base commit of the pull request.
rows.default: Unset: no default. The step sets the variable in its own `env` block on every run.
rows.effect: The step passes it to `bin/ci/generate_benchmark_report.sh` as the third argument, the reference commit. The report adds a comparison with that commit when a file `/scratch/tron-benchmark/<7-character commit id>.*.json` exists.
rows.notes: The script replaces the value with the head of `BASE_REF` when it finds that branch on the remote. It then uses the merge commit of the pull request with that head commit, when one exists. The step passes empty text when `BASE_REF` equals `DEFAULT_BRANCH`.

rows.name: BENCHMARK_ENVIRONMENT_STORE_PATH
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py`, `bin/ci/nix-cache/publish_lab.py`, step `Restore exact Nix benchmark runtime` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Path that resolves through symbolic links to one Nix store path. The resolved text must have the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`.
rows.default: Unset: `publish_lab.py` ends with `KeyError`. `prepare_handoff.py` requires the option `--benchmark-environment`. Empty: both scripts apply the store path check to the current directory.
rows.effect: `prepare_handoff.py` writes the resolved path to its step outputs. It also computes `BENCHMARK_PAYLOAD_IDENTITY` from the path. `publish_lab.py` passes the path to `nix-instantiate`. It queues the result for the lab Nix cache with `/usr/local/bin/tron-nix-cache-enqueue`.
rows.notes: The benchmark environment is the Nix output with `bin/python3` and `bin/uv` for the benchmark job. The option `--benchmark-environment` replaces the variable in `prepare_handoff.py`. `benchmark_runtime.py prepare` in the benchmark job accepts only the store path itself. `LAB_NIX_CACHE` holds the address of the lab Nix cache.

rows.name: BENCHMARK_PAYLOAD_IDENTITY
rows.read_by: Steps `Restore exact Nix benchmark runtime` and `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Other text gives the message `invalid benchmark payload identity` and exit status 2.
rows.default: Unset: no default. Both steps set it from the output `benchmark_payload_identity` of job `tron-build`.
rows.effect: `bin/ci/tron-build/benchmark_runtime.py prepare` stops when the value differs from the hash of the two store paths that it receives. `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` includes the value in the identity of the cached benchmark result.
rows.notes: The value is the SHA-256 hash of the two benchmark store paths (runtime and environment). `run_benchmark.sh` reuses a cached result when the value, `SOURCE_HASH`, `MACHINE_CLASS` and the host all match. A run attempt above 1 disables the reuse.

rows.name: BOT_BRANCH
rows.read_by: Step `Dispatch required CI for refresh PR` of job `publish` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
rows.values: Branch name of the form `bot/slice-cost-data-<platform>`. The step sets it from the output `branch` of the step `refresh_pr`.

rows.name: BOT_HEAD_SHA
rows.read_by: Step `Dispatch required CI for refresh PR` of job `publish` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
rows.values: Git commit id of 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The step sets it from the output `head_sha` of the step `refresh_pr`.
rows.default: Unset: no default. An empty value stops `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` with the message `bot head SHA is required`.

rows.name: BUILD_ARTIFACT_MAX_AGE_DAYS
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/ci-cleanup-build-artifacts.sh`
rows.values: Whole number of days, digits only. Other text stops the script with the message `BUILD_ARTIFACT_MAX_AGE_DAYS must be an integer` and exit status 2.
rows.default: Unset: 3 days. An empty value also gives 3 days.
rows.effect: The script removes build artifact directories whose modification time is at least this many days old. It looks only at directories named with 7 lowercase hexadecimal characters, at most 2 levels below the artifact root.
rows.notes: The artifact root is the first argument of the script (default `/scratch/tron-build`). With `0` the script removes directories of any age. Bash reads a leading `0` as octal: `010` means 8 days, and `08` is an arithmetic error.

rows.name: BUILD_INPUTS_STORE_PATH
rows.read_by: Steps `Wait for complete build plan` and `Acquire build plan` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Nix store path of the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`. The jobs set it from the output `store_path` of job `prepare-tron-build-inputs`.
rows.default: Unset: no default. The jobs `wait-for-lab-cache` and `tron-build` set it in their `env` blocks.
rows.effect: It names the build plan (the Nix output with the build recipe and the tool environments). `bin/ci/nix-cache/wait.py` waits until the lab Nix cache holds it. `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py` copies it from that cache.
rows.notes: Text that is not a Nix store path stops both scripts with an argument error. Each script waits at most 2700 seconds (45 minutes). The lab Nix cache is the Nix binary cache at `LAB_NIX_CACHE`.

rows.default: Unset: the step fails. The step sets the variable in its own `env` block on every run.

rows.name: CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S
rows.who_sets: No file in the repository sets it.
rows.read_by: `bin/fuse_cleanup.py`
rows.values: Positive number (`10`, `0.5`) with an optional unit: `s` seconds, `m` minutes, `h` hours, `d` days. No unit means seconds. Zero or other text stops the program (exit status 2).

rows.name: COVERAGE_CABAL_FLAGS
rows.read_by: Steps `Build with coverage` and `Check built ingest binaries have no bare -N (regression guard, #3087)` of job `ingest-coverage` (`.github/workflows/ingest-coverage.yml`)
rows.values: Options for cabal (the Haskell build tool that builds ingest). The shell splits the text at spaces. The workflow writes `--enable-coverage --disable-optimization --builddir=dist-newstyle/coverage/cabal`.
rows.default: Unset: no default. The workflow sets it in its top-level `env` block.
rows.effect: The steps add these options to `$CABAL_INSTALL build` and `$CABAL_INSTALL list-bin`. The options turn coverage on, turn optimization off and set the build directory.
rows.notes: The `make` steps of the same job use the make variable `COVERAGE_CABAL_FLAGS` of `ingest/Makefile`. The Makefile assigns that variable with `:=` and does not take it from the environment. Both places hold the same options.

rows.name: CPUS_PER_MACHINE
rows.read_by: Step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Positive whole number without a leading zero. The step sets it from the matrix value `cpus_per_machine`: `192` for the class `2x96core`, `144` for the class `2x72core`.
rows.default: Unset: no default. An empty value stops `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` with exit status 2.
rows.effect: The step passes it to `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh` as the last argument. That script passes it to `bin/ci/benchmark_save.py` as `--cpus-per-machine`. The benchmark stops when the machine has a different count of physical CPU cores.
rows.notes: `bin/ci/ci-run-benchmark.sh` and `bin/ci/benchmark_save.py` have their own variables of the same name. They do not read the environment variable. `benchmark_save.py` divides the count equally among the benchmark instances. A reused cached result skips `benchmark_save.py`.

rows.name: DEB_VERSION
rows.read_by: Step `Require the feature build below the testing candidate` of job `verify-testing-order` (`.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml`)
rows.values: Debian package version. The step sets it from the output `deb_version` of job `build`. The check accepts only a version that contains `~feature.`.
rows.default: Unset: no default. An empty value stops `bin/ci/check-feature-below-candidate.sh` with exit status 2.
rows.effect: The step passes it to `bin/ci/check-feature-below-candidate.sh` as the version of the built `tron` package. The script succeeds only when it sorts below the highest non-feature version in the `testing` channel.
rows.notes: A feature build is a package whose version contains `~feature.`. A channel is one package repository on the APT server. `GNUmakefile` and `cmake/SetVersion.cmake` compute variables of the same name themselves. They do not read this variable.

rows.name: DEFAULT_BRANCH
rows.read_by: `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`, inline steps of the 4 workflows that set it
rows.values: Branch name. The 4 workflows write `${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}`, the default branch of the repository. The readers use the text unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` uses `main`. An empty value gives the same result.

notes: All 21 names are kept and none is dropped. Every evidence site was opened at commit 7eddde7895 and every quote equals its source line. 13 rows have at least one edited cell and 8 rows are unchanged (APT_DEPLOY_KEY, APT_SSH_KEY, APT_SSH_USER, BOT_BRANCH, BOT_HEAD_SHA, BUILD_INPUTS_STORE_PATH, DEB_VERSION, DEFAULT_BRANCH). The largest corrections: COVERAGE_CABAL_FLAGS default (the second step uses `set -u`), the two BENCHMARK_*_STORE_PATH rows (empty value, and the program that queues paths for the lab Nix cache), BASE_SHA (the condition for the comparison) and the reader of CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S (`bin/fuse_cleanup.py`, not the wrapper script, which the notes cell now names). DEFAULT_BRANCH keeps 'workflow env' with mixed levels, and BUILD_INPUTS_STORE_PATH keeps 'workflow env' for a job-level entry. DEB_VERSION keeps the test line as evidence, since the workflow line that calls the script contains a pipe character. Two statements rest on language behaviour outside the checkout: Bash octal reading in BUILD_ARTIFACT_MAX_AGE_DAYS and argparse default conversion in CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S. Both were checked with separate small commands, not with repository scripts. One term was added to new_terms: `reference commit`, used by BASE_REF and BASE_SHA (bin/ci/generate_benchmark_report.sh:19 describes the argument as the commit to compare against).
